author: ShadowPit
text:
Naveen - 5 years and I have not mastered it yet.

Whenever - Sometimes I will draw a line of best fit through S/R based on how price is reacting at a level and my risk appetite. I recommend you don't follow this (this is simply how I am tuned to the market, how I pinpoint the imbalance in the supply and demand equation). The logic is based on how price reacted specifically to those lines, I asked questions like where did price originate from when it tanked, where couldn't the cluster close above, where couldn't the cluster close below. The entry was based on minimising risk as much as possible, and getting in where price couldn't previously close above on this timeframe.

author: ShadowPit
text:
Further to that GJ analysis, you should be aware of all the options you have on how to trade it. Have fun finding out what works for you and what your actual appetite to risk really is. There is so much more to finding that 'perfect' entry. How long can you really hold onto your trade for optimal R:R?

Hopefully now you can see that making pips means almost jack shit, and its how you manage your appetite for risk, acceptance of losses, and what kind of lot size you're able to leverage into any given trade. Think larger sample sizes (100's of trades), and tweak and adjust your trading behaviours to what you feel 'comfortable' wearing.

How many of you have had iron discipline for hundreds of trades and analysed the results? I bet only a very small handful of you!

author: ShadowPit
text:
Thanks whynotnaveen,

There is absolutely nothing wrong with 20pip stop losses or 2.5R as you're learning about trading and getting comfortable with what works for YOU! If you were to critically review your trading you just might find out some interesting things about your decisions and trading behaviour. It just might be possible to extract more from your trades than you realise, perhaps you're always entering too early (touch trade large zones)...or too late (chasing price after its reacted). In the right context a 20 pip stop loss could mean a 200 pip win if using a D1 zone but M15/M30 precision entries, that's 10:1! Or perhaps you're not drilling down enough into the zone and discovering the more precise entry with a tighter stop loss 10-15 pips, both on the entry and exit, which could potentially turn your 2.5R into a 4R trade. There are a lot of factors you have control over:) The power of self review should not be underestimated.

Good luck!

author: smimon
text:
kxfx wrote: Sir ShadowPit,

When you have the time, is it possible for you to tell me how your morning ritual is? I mean, how you start your trading morning/day? Mine is always chaotic when I was monitoring multiple pairs (10 pairs). How did you start your day and still could scalp beautifully, when you are monitoring more than 15 (or 20)?

Big salute for your Monday trades. I've always thought Monday is a bad day for trade. I'm not confidence even with London session as I thought the ITs are still sleeping

I know you didn't direct this at me, but I also monitor a large number of pairs - the way I manage it is as follows: - I always only ever have one chart at a time fullscreened - I condense my view (zoom out a lot) - you need to be able to see as much context as possible at all times, to get a feel for the big picture - widescreen monitors are not good for this, it squashes all the PA too much vertically.

Either use a monitor with a more square aspect ratio, or use the fixed chart scale option a lot to stretch things out vertically - the more vertically exaggerated the PA, the easier it is to read - I cycle through each chart first thing in the morning on M15/H1, and mark the nearest levels that I want to look for trades at above and below where price currently is - you MUST use alerts if you want to trade this many instruments. Many times, it's just a case of marking the best levels above/below price for each chart. setting alerts, and then just waiting for price to reach them. The main benefit to trading this many instruments is that you can trade only the more significant levels without too much waiting in between. Something usually hits something halfway significant every hour or two - I either play some computer game whilst I wait, or I just randomly click through each chart if I am bored, and cycle timeframes, to see if there are any scalps available that catch my eye
